title: Shadow Experiments: Data Handling and Redaction Policy
author: Marcus Lin
body:
> **Archived 2026-01-14:** this page is superseded by "Shadow Traffic: Data Retention, Redaction, and Residency Policy" and is kept for reference only.

## Purpose
This policy sets out how Redwood Inference handles data produced by Shadow Experiments (Shadow Traffic). It describes:
- Which data is captured and which is not
- Default retention and deletion
- Redaction and truncation of prompts and outputs
- Customer controls and opt-outs
- Dedicated and Private configuration options
- Residency constraints

Shadow Experiments mirror a sampled share of production requests to one or more shadow variants, score the outputs asynchronously and report quality metrics without touching the user-facing response. The policy covers data from shadow request mirroring, shadow pair telemetry, scoring/eval outputs and Console example drilldowns.

## Scope and definitions
### Shadow artifacts
1) Shadow Pair Telemetry Event: links a control request/response to its shadow request/responses.
2) Shadow Content Payload: prompt/context and output content (or redacted versions) kept for scoring and drilldown.
3) Scoring Output: heuristic and model-graded metric values plus rubric version, evaluator model ID and payload references.
4) Console Example Drilldown Material: a small, access-controlled sample of pairs shown in Console for debugging.

### Out of scope
- Offline replay of historical traffic beyond the retention windows.
- Customer-supplied code execution inside Redwood.

### Classification
Shadow artifacts typically carry customer content and are Customer Confidential. Prompts can include PII, PHI, secrets, regulated financial data or auth tokens. Any artifact holding raw prompt/output text is "Customer Content — Restricted".

## Principles
1) Minimize data by default.
2) Safe defaults; Dedicated/Private may request more, subject to security review and contract.
3) Fail-open: redaction or storage failures must never affect the user response path.
4) Residency-preserving: no cross-region replication of raw content.
5) Tenant- and role-scoped access with auditing.

## What we capture by default
### Hosted API
A) Always-on metadata: HMAC request fingerprint, internal tenant ID, route/experiment/variant IDs, timing, timeout flags, error classes, token counts.

B) Content payloads: raw text is not persisted. We keep redacted/truncated prompt and output snippets for format checks and, optionally, hashed n-gram features for dedupe and clustering.

### Dedicated
As Hosted, plus customer-configurable retention and example sampling, and optional expanded debug capture (explicit enablement, admin role).

### Private
We recommend no raw content persistence. If the customer turns it on, storage stays in the customer environment under their retention settings.

## Retention policy
"Retention" is the maximum time data stays accessible in primary storage; afterwards it is deleted or irreversibly transformed.

### Default retention table
Artifact type | Hosted default | Dedicated default | Private default
---|---:|---:|---:
Shadow Pair Telemetry (metadata only) | 14 days | 30 days | Customer-controlled
Shadow Content Payload (redacted) | 72 hours | 7 days | Customer-controlled
Shadow Content Payload (raw, if enabled) | Disabled | Disabled | Disabled
Scoring Output (metrics only) | 90 days | 180 days | Customer-controlled
Console Example Drilldown (redacted) | 7 days | 14 days | Customer-controlled

Retention is enforced with storage-layer TTLs where available and a daily deletion job that verifies deletion.

### Extended retention
Only for Dedicated or Private, and only with Security Engineering + Compliance Product review, a documented purpose, customer admin enablement in Console, and confirmation that the residency region supports the storage class.

### Legal hold
Shadow artifacts are not designed for legal hold; requests go through Finance/Legal and Security, and preservation is not guaranteed.

### Deletion
- Hosted: disabling shadow testing stops capture immediately; existing data expires via TTL; emergency deletion via Support for security incidents.
- Dedicated: tenant admins can request an immediate purge; Support-assisted purge is also available.
- Private: customer-controlled.

Purge targets (Hosted/Dedicated):
- Disable capture: < 5 minutes
- Content payload purge: < 24 hours
- Scoring outputs purge: < 72 hours

## Redaction and transformation
Default is redact + truncate + minimize; raw storage is off.

Stage 0: Pre-ingestion filtering. Skip capture when the request has x-redwood-no-capture: true, the tenant policy is shadow_capture = none, or the classification is "restricted: no content retention".

Stage 1: Structural extraction. For chat, tool calls and JSON schema outputs we keep role labels, message boundaries, tool names (not arguments) and schema keys (not values).

Stage 2: Pattern redaction. Emails, phone numbers, national IDs, PAN-like numbers, API keys/tokens ("sk-…", "Bearer …", JWT-like strings) and header tokens are replaced with tags such as [REDACTED_EMAIL] or [REDACTED_TOKEN], with stable per-tenant hashes for repeated values.

Stage 3: Truncation. Default caps:
- Prompt snippet: max 2,000 characters OR 512 tokens (whichever is smaller)
- Output snippet: max 2,000 characters OR 512 tokens
For streaming, only the final assembled output is captured; on failure we store "[TRUNCATED_STREAM_OUTPUT]" and token counts.

Stage 4: analytics_only. No snippets at all; only token counts, format compliance booleans, aggregated rubric scores, fingerprints and metadata.

### Tool/function calls
Tool names are kept; arguments are never stored as raw text. We keep argument keys, args_valid_json and the schema validation result.

### Customer identifiers
end_user_id, prompt_id and conversation_id are stored only as tenant-scoped HMAC hashes, optionally with a coarse bucket.

### Limitations
Redaction is best-effort. Highly regulated customers should use Dedicated/Private with analytics_only or disable capture. Finding raw sensitive data in artifacts is a security incident and must be escalated immediately.

## Customer controls
1) shadow_capture_mode: none | redacted_snippets (default) | analytics_only
2) retention_overrides for metadata, snippets and scoring outputs, within the maxima below
3) example_drilldown_enabled: false recommended for sensitive tenants; true by default for dogfood/beta tenants
4) Opt-out headers: x-redwood-no-capture: true and x-redwood-no-shadow: true

### Hard maxima (Hosted/Dedicated)
Without Security approval and a contract addendum:
- No raw content retention
- Snippets no longer than 30 days
- Example drilldowns no longer than 30 days
- Scoring outputs no longer than 365 days

### Console requirements
Show capture mode and retention, warn that redaction is best-effort, require acknowledgement for drilldowns, and offer "Disable shadow testing" and "Request purge" actions.

## Residency
- Artifacts are stored and processed in the tenant's region/realm.
- Scoring runs in-region; no cross-region scoring when snippets exist.
- With analytics_only and no content, cross-region metric aggregation is allowed only if the residency contract permits.
- Private: everything stays in the customer environment; Redwood ships rubric templates as packages only.
- Backups: content snippets use backup exclusion where possible; otherwise backup retention must not exceed the snippet TTL.

## Access, audit and encryption
- Drilldown access: Tenant Admin, Security Admin (tenant), and the optional Quality Analyst role (Dedicated). Redwood internal access only via break-glass with a ticket.
- Audit log entries (actor, tenant, timestamp, action, prior and new value) for enable/disable, capture mode or retention changes, drilldown toggles, experiment changes, and purges.
- TLS 1.2+ in transit; tenant-scoped keys at rest where supported.

## Dedicated and Private knobs
### Dedicated
- capture_mode: none | redacted_snippets | analytics_only
- snippet_retention_days: 1–14 (default 3)
- metadata_retention_days: 7–90 (default 30)
- scoring_retention_days: 30–365 (default 180)
- example_drilldown_enabled: true/false
- example_sample_rate: 0.0–0.05 (default 0.005)
- residency_region: pinned to the Dedicated cluster region

### Private
- storage_backend and retention_policy: customer-managed (required)
- capture_mode: customer choice (analytics_only recommended)
- siem_export: optional

## Implementation must-haves
1) TTLs on every content-bearing table/object; idempotent deletion jobs with metrics.
2) Content snippets stored separately from metrics/metadata.
3) redacted_snippets with short retention by default on Hosted; analytics_only for flagged high-sensitivity tenants.
4) Per-tenant capture kill switch and a global drilldown kill switch.
5) Metrics for snippet vs analytics_only share, redaction errors, purge success/latency and cross-region access attempts.

## Exceptions
Raw content storage, retention beyond maxima or cross-region processing with content requires written approval from Security Engineering (Marcus Lin) and Compliance Product (Naomi Feldman), exec sponsor sign-off (Priya Natarajan), and contract documentation where customer-facing.

## Procedures
### Tenant purge (Hosted/Dedicated)
1) Confirm requester authorization with Support and the tenant admin.
2) Flip the tenant kill switch.
3) Purge the content payload store, drilldown cache and, if requested, scoring outputs.
4) Verify via purge metrics and spot checks.
5) Update the ticket with audit log IDs.

### Enabling drilldowns (Dedicated)
1) capture_mode must not be none.
2) Snippet retention must be <= 14 days.
3) Tenant admin acknowledges in Console.
4) RBAC roles configured.
5) Audit logs flowing to the tenant sink if configured.
